quarterly_data.signal: September 2026 quarter, fifth consecutive record (CFO Doug Bettinger, non-GAAP): revenue $8.22 billion, up 22% sequentially and 54% year over year; gross margin a record 52.4% (52% in June) on favorable customer and product mix; operating expenses $1 billion versus $916 million (higher incentive compensation; investment in Akara, Halo, panel form factors and Dextro; R&D about two-thirds of opex); operating margin a record 40.2%, above 40% for the first time; tax rate 16.5% (expected to stay in this range); diluted EPS a record $2.20. Customer Support Business Group revenue a fourth consecutive record at nearly $2.5 billion, 40% higher year over year. Deferred revenue $2.66 billion (+$227 million); free cash flow a record $3.24 billion; cash and short-term investments $7.5 billion; inventory $4.6 billion (+$274 million, built for expected demand) with turns of 3.4x, the highest in nearly seven years; capex $258 million (lab infrastructure and global manufacturing expansion); about 24,300 regular full-time employees, up about 1,900 in the quarter, mainly factory and field.
quarterly_data.figure: Sept-quarter revenue $8.22 billion (+54% YoY); gross margin 52.4%; operating margin 40.2%; EPS $2.20

quarterly_data.signal: September-quarter mix (CFO Doug Bettinger): memory 46% of systems revenue, a record in dollars and up 120% year over year; non-volatile memory 26% (23% in June), with NAND revenue up approximately 40% sequentially on conversions to 256-layer and above devices and initial spending on 384-layer class devices; DRAM 20% (23%), a record in dollars, focused on 1-alpha, 1-beta and 1-gamma nodes enabling DDR5, LPDDR5 and high-bandwidth memory; foundry a record 46% (44%), on leading-edge nodes including advanced packaging and mature-node spending in China; logic and other 8% (10%). By region China was 35% of revenue (26% in June), Korea 20% and Taiwan 18% (27%); the CFO expects China to be 'meaningfully down' as a percentage in the December quarter, driven by domestic customers, while multinationals in China stay reasonably strong. CEO Tim Archer: foundry logic and DRAM have accounted for approximately 80% of Lam's systems revenue growth year to date.
quarterly_data.figure: memory 46% of systems revenue (+120% YoY); foundry 46%; China 35% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook: December 2026 quarter revenue $8.6 billion plus or minus $400 million (CFO: 'would have been a bit higher if not for some near-term supply chain constraints'; delayed shipments move to the March quarter), gross margin 52.5% plus or minus 1 point, operating margin 40.5% plus or minus 1 point, EPS $2.33 plus or minus $0.15 on about 1.253 billion shares. CEO Tim Archer: calendar 2026 systems revenue expected to grow well over 40%; CY2026 WFE in the mid $150 billion range and a preliminary 2027 WFE outlook of more than $200 billion, growth led by DRAM, then leading-edge foundry logic and NAND, with customer visibility through 2028; 2026 would be Lam's third consecutive year of WFE outperformance. CSBG revenue expected to grow more than 30% in CY2026 and over 15% in CY2027. Cumulative Aether dry resist revenue now expected at approximately $2.5 billion by the end of the decade, roughly $1 billion above the prior expectation. CFO: advanced packaging growth of 70% 'for this year is still the right number'; gross margin to stay near current levels near term, with mid-50s the multi-year aim; 10 new tier I fabs come online next year; mature-node spending outside China expected to be strong next year.
quarterly_data.figure: Dec-quarter revenue $8.6 billion +/- $400 million; 2027 WFE >$200 billion; CY2026 systems revenue growth well over 40%; Aether ~$2.5 billion cumulative by the end of the decade

quarterly_data.signal: Supply (CEO Tim Archer, CFO Doug Bettinger): into 2027 'clean room space availability and supply chain constraints for certain components' continue to limit chip makers' and equipment companies' ability to fully meet end demand; 2026 was primarily clean-room constrained. Lam saw 'a little bit of tightness' in its supply chain in the quarter, which held back the December guide; it is working with suppliers to accelerate their capacity expansion and hosted 'a couple of big events' with its global suppliers in the last two months. CEO: 'this is nothing like' the COVID shortages; some suppliers, for example in advanced packaging, see Lam's demand on them rising much faster than Lam itself, and 'we'll be caught up very shortly'. CFO: Lam would be open to investing in suppliers if needed but many are well capitalized, and it is building inventory for next year's demand.

Product wins (CEO Tim Archer): Lam recently secured tool of record wins for Vector, Sabre, Flex and Halo (molybdenum) backside power processes at a leading customer ramping backside power at 2 nanometer and below. In advanced packaging Syndion attained four new positions across multiple customers in advanced logic and HBM TSV, Striker ALD won multiple TSV liner positions, and Vector and VECTOR TEOS 3D won high-adhesion bonding film and interdie gap fill applications. Panel plating systems have shipped to more than 20 customers across panel sizes from 300 by 300 millimeter to 600 by 600 millimeter (Kallisto platform, also positioned for through-glass vias in glass core substrates), and Lam expects its panel-level packaging share to surpass its wafer-level packaging share. Equipment Intelligence and Dextro cobots helped secure performance-based service contracts with multiple memory manufacturers. Akara delivers up to a 50% reduction in wafer-to-wafer and lot-to-lot variability and up to a 50% gain in wafer output per fab footprint; Aether has shown sub-10 nanometer resolution with High-NA EUV at 10% lower exposure dose and is ramping in HBM high volume manufacturing with Low-NA EUV.
quarterly_data.figure: tool of record wins for four products at a leading customer; four new Syndion positions; panel plating systems at more than 20 customers

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Tim Archer's views: rising deposition and etch intensity has expanded Lam's served available market by four points as a percentage of WFE over the past few years; on DRAM roadmaps, 'if really we're making a leap right from 6F2 into 3D DRAM, then etch and dep intensity is going to rise even faster', while extending today's architecture drives advanced patterning (Aether, Akara); under Lam's model of $100 billion of AI capex being about $10 billion of WFE, Lam's opportunity within that $10 billion is greater next year because of device evolution. The 2x foundry logic SAM per wafer laid out at the 2025 Analyst Day is 'maybe halfway through'. CFO Doug Bettinger: the 2027 WFE ranking has not changed with newly announced logic fab projects, which Lam knew about in advance; unconstrained 2027 demand 'would be higher'.
quarterly_data.figure: SAM up four points as a percentage of WFE; $100 billion AI capex ~ $10 billion WFE

players.product: high-aspect-ratio dielectric etch & cryogenic etch tools for NAND stacks

quarterly_data.signal: NAND storage tiers (CEO Tim Archer): AI is driving multiple NAND tiers, QLC for cost-effective capacity, TLC as a high-bandwidth tier for context memory and KV cache, and SLC class NAND emerging for low-latency agentic AI; converting TLC to SLC class devices reduces bits per device by roughly 3 times, so each percentage point of NAND bit mix shifting to SLC class needs approximately 2% more installed wafer capacity for the same bit demand, which the CEO believes could become 'a meaningful driver of NAND wafer capacity' (too early to size the SLC share). Lam has the industry's largest installed base of NAND systems. The upgrade cycle from 128-layer to 200-layer class devices is to finish in 2027, rolling into the next upgrade cycle as customers move to 300 and 400-layer devices; CFO Doug Bettinger: both upgrades and new equipment were meaningful contributors to NAND growth.
quarterly_data.figure: each 1 point of NAND bits shifting to SLC needs approximately 2% more installed wafer capacity; TLC to SLC cuts bits per device roughly 3x
